author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Thai Formula Two driver Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak escaped without injury after his car crashed and caught fire during Friday practice at Madrid’s new Madring circuit. The accident was the first major crash of the Spanish Grand Prix weekend.

The 20-year-old lost control at turn 19 and spun backward into the barriers. Flames spread through the wreckage, but Inthraphuvasak climbed out of the cockpit without assistance and made his way over the wall, Reuters reported.

Officials stopped the session with a red flag. Marshals took time to reach the car with extinguishers, and the track was not cleared for about 24 minutes. Practice resumed with only six minutes remaining, sharply limiting running for the rest of the field.

The crash occurred before Formula One cars began their own work at the newly built street circuit. Drivers had already raised questions about risks associated with the venue. Inthraphuvasak’s quick exit prevented injury, but the fire and response time will give organizers and racing officials clear evidence to review as the weekend continues.
dek: Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak climbed from his burning car without assistance after hitting the barriers during practice in Madrid.
headline: Thai Formula Two driver escapes fiery Madring crash
